components.notes: Compared item by item with preprint Section 2, pp. 3-8: countably infinite P; atoms, literals, positive and negative literals, bar involution (p. 5); the S forms (2) and glosses (3); the remark that S contains the forms with a negated first literal that are equivalent to positive-subject forms (handbook lines 55-56); the S-dagger forms (4) and the genuinely new negated-subject forms (lines 53-54); the formula bar and fragment closure (p. 6); nonempty domain, literal complement, truth conditions, satisfiability and consequence, no existential commitment of universals (p. 7); absurdities, formula negation and the two identifications (p. 8). Failure condition does not hold: lines 44-46 exclude Boolean structure; lines 53-56, annex lines 15-20 and lines 325-327 confine genuinely negative subjects to S-dagger.

components.gap: Supply the Section 3 lemmas with the source's hypotheses and every case their statements promise. Preprint Lemmas 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 (pp. 14-15) are stated for a set Phi of universal formulas. Definition def:p02-syllogistic-literal-closure and Lemmas thm:p02-syllogistic-closure and thm:p02-syllogistic-extension (handbook/parts/p02/syllogistic-inference.tex lines 171-196) drop that hypothesis, and Lemma thm:p02-syllogistic-extension asserts that a complete extension defines a one-element structure satisfying an arbitrary Phi. Its annex proof (handbook/annex/p02/syllogistic-inference.tex lines 212-218) checks universal premises only, so the promised case of existential members of Phi is not proved, and the handbook's own Lemma thm:p02-w02c-p02-002-existential-closure refutes the statement for Phi = {\exists(p,q)}. Restrict Phi to universal formulas in that definition and those lemmas, as in the source. The file is a read-only host for this packet and for the unit's owner packet, so the change needs a lead patch. The Section 3 claims that A, T and I have no classical counterparts, that T is needed to derive \forall(p,p) from no premises, that D2 and B are classical forms and X is ex falso quodlibet, and that D1 is kept for ease of use and for the relation to the system R (preprint pp. 12-13) are present only in the owned files, which are not yet on the route.

defect_observations: Lemma thm:p02-syllogistic-extension (handbook/parts/p02/syllogistic-inference.tex lines 191-196) is stated for an arbitrary Phi, while Lemma thm:p02-w02c-p02-002-existential-closure (owned body lines 136-150) shows it fails for Phi = {\exists(p,q)}; the owned text (lines 32-36, 128-134) describes the lemmas as restricted to universal premises, which the statements do not say. Verdict-changing for LR001-C2.

The two S-dagger glosses of preprint p. 4 (Some non-p is not a q; Every non-p is a q) are not given in words; lines 53-54 name the forms only. Not verdict-changing: glosses are not part of the C1 success condition.

The preprint's remark (p. 7) that semantic consequence is a rational reconstruction of the pre-theoretic judgment of valid inference is not reproduced. Not verdict-changing: a framing remark outside the definitions extent of C1.
Example def:p02-syllogistic-negative-witness derives the source's sequent (13) by D2 then D1, whereas the source's derivation on p. 9 uses D1 twice with a silent identification. Not a gap.
